title: Automated Canary Gate and Safety-Revert for Quantized Calibration Failures
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Goal: Implement an automated canary gating mechanism and safety-revert policy for FP8 and INT8 quantized model variants that fail calibration/accuracy validation during canary traffic. The feature must allow the serving control plane to promote a quantized model only if calibration and accuracy checks pass on a small live traffic slice, and to automatically and safely fallback to a compatible float/less-quantized variant when detected regressions exceed defined thresholds. This ticket covers orchestration, calibration harness integration, metric gating, rollback automation, and alerting (no UI changes).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Canary promotion pipeline runs per-deployment calibration checks (calibration harness + live-applied evals) before marking quantized variant as healthy. 2) If accuracy or perf thresholds are violated in the canary window, traffic must be shifted to the previous approved variant with 0 dropped requests and no increased 5xx rate. 3) The system produces an audit entry with the failing metrics, calibration artifacts link, and the exact fallback decision. 4) Ops can force override/pin a variant. 5) Unit & e2e tests exercising the gating and rollback logic are present in CI.
implementation_notes: - Integrate the calibration harness (calib-harness service) to run a short, deterministic calibration + validation job when a quantized variant is deployed to canary. - Extend canary controller to accept a 'quant-gate' step: run harness + evaluate metrics produced by harness and live evals. - Metrics considered: task-specific accuracy (exact match/accuracy), delta in perplexity on held-out eval set, and distributional checks on logits (KL divergence vs float baseline) to catch catastrophic shifts. - Thresholds: FP8: absolute accuracy drop <= 0.5% and perplexity change <= 3%; INT8: absolute accuracy drop <= 1.0% and perplexity change <= 5%. Live-monitoring tolerance: same thresholds but measured over 15-minute sliding window. - Rollback flow: initiate atomic routing change to previous variant, mark quantized variant as 'failed-qa', store calibration artifacts (calibration histogram, scale params), and tag variant with failure reason. - Backoff policy for reattempts: require manual requeue for retrain/recalib if variant fails twice within 7 days. - Preserve KV cache compatibility: when fallback occurs, ensure routing preserves cache keys where possible or gracefully warms cache to avoid latency spikes.
test_plan: - Unit tests for gating logic (threshold evaluation, artifact persistence). - Integration test: deploy a canary quantized model, inject simulated metric deltas from harness, assert automatic rollback. - Staging canary smoke: run on staging with small % of synthetic traffic and intentionally corrupted calibration artifact to verify detection. - Load test: ensure routing switch has <200ms median additional latency and no request loss. - Regression tests added for calibration harness output schema changes.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag behind 'quant_canary_gate' (default off). 2) Enable in staging and run 2 full cycles (calibration + live eval) — target date 2026-03-18. 3) Canary rollout to <1% production traffic for a subset of models (internal experiment) for 2 days. 4) Gradually increase to 5% if no failures. 5) Monitor and then flip flag company-wide — target by 2026-03-28. Manual rollback procedures documented for first two weeks.
monitoring: Dashboards: quant-canary-gate (per-model), canary-failure-rate, auto-revert-counts, avg-routing-switch-latency. Alerts: P0 if auto-revert rate > 0.5% for any model over 1h; P1 if canary validation errors occur repeatedly for same model. Log fields: variant_id, calibration_job_id, metric_snapshot_url, decision_reason. Store artifacts in s3://redwood-calib-artifacts/{model}/{variant}/{timestamp}/.
blockers: - Need updated calibration harness API contract (ENG-16911) to expose KL/logit distribution outputs. - Approval for thresholds from applied-ml and product (pending meeting 2026-03-12).
comments: 2026-03-10 Aisha Kaur: Initial RFC posted. Focus should be on fast deterministic validation runs under 60s for canary. Linked design doc.

2026-03-11 Luis Martinez: Spike showed we can run calib + eval in ~45s on c5-large worker with cached activations. Need to ensure we surface 'trusted' metrics: prefer exact-match and perplexity over soft similarity metrics for gating.

2026-03-12 Priya Desai: SRE okay with automated routing switches as long as there's a circuit-breaker and we emit detailed audit logs. We should add a short cooldown (60s) before allowing another automatic revert for the same model.
2026-03-13 Marco Rossi: Product approved the rollout plan pending two staging cycles and final threshold sign-off. Add a customer-impact tag to audit records so we can filter by enterprise customers.
2026-03-13 Luis Martinez: Implemented prototype controller changes and added unit tests. Pushed PR to servicing and calib-harness. Requesting review from Aisha and Priya.
